title: How to Make AI Ads
summary: How to make AI ads that feel like short films: 6 steps from brief to edit, with the real prompts behind two client ads made in Flick.
body_markdown:
## How to make an AI ad in 6 steps


Each step works for any ad. "With AI" shows how it was done in Flick, with the real prompts from The Ghosted Boss and Pond Marketing video.


### 1. Write a timed brief before you generate anything


**What it is:** a page that says what happens in every second of the ad: the action, the camera and every line of dialogue, in order.


**Why it matters:** the story has to fit 30 seconds, and every shot needs a job. A brief also tells the model when each line lands.


How to do it


- Write your basic idea in one sentence: whose day changes, and how.
- Split the length into timed beats, one line each.
- For dialogue, write who speaks, what they say and when the camera moves.


With AI


The Ghosted Boss is one continuous take, so its brief is the conversation: what the boss says, what the off-screen AI team answers, and when the camera pulls back. The final video prompt keeps it line by line.


Model: Seedance 2.5 Final · Note: the final take's prompt, in full


```text
First, CEO wearing red sweater twirls a pen in his hand. Then, the camera cuts to a close-up of him speaking directly to the camera.He confidently asks:
"how's the automation going?"
** WOMAN Voiceover:** "Done, sir."


The camera slowly begins to pull back.


**7–15s — The Team**


The CEO continues:
"Operations?"


**MAN Voiceover:** "All workflows running."


**CEO:** "Customer support?"


**WOMAN Voiceover:** "Handled."
CAMERA CONTINUE pull back


THERE ARE dozens of empty chairs.


He nods confidently.


**CEO:** "Great work, everyone."


He feel relaxed.


NO BACKGROUND MUSIC
```


### 2. Pick a look to borrow from a film you love


Zoey Z.


, director of[Pond Marketing video](https://flick.art/film/pond-marketing-video-f4dc6d)


**What it is:** a set of stills whose palette, lenses and production design you want the ad to share.


**Why it matters:** the visuals can look like live action and still feel like an ad. A film's look is what makes them read as cinema.


How to do it


- Collect a few stills from a film or show you like, or screenshots from YouTube.
- Keep to one look, so every shot shares one grade.


With AI


The Ghosted Boss used[Flickpedia](https://flick.art/flickpedia) 's Cinematic vintage style on its character sheets and set designs. Pond Marketing video's lead began as the Flickpedia still above. Flickpedia is Flick's library of visual styles and film references, and you can upload your own stills to the canvas too.


### 3. Make a character sheet, then dress it in the product


Zoey Z.


, director of[The Ghosted Boss](https://flick.art/film/the-ghosted-boss-383dd2)


· GPT Image 2.5


**What it is:** a turnaround sheet of your lead, front, side and back on a plain background, plus a sheet of facial expressions.


**Why it matters:** every later shot copies the same face and clothes from it, so the character stays one person across the ad.


How to do it


- Generate a few faces and keep the one you would remember.
- Turn it into a turnaround sheet, then a sheet of six expressions for close-ups.
- To dress the character in a real product, attach a photo of it and say exactly what to replace and what to keep.


With AI


The Ghosted Boss started in a three piece suit. Zoey swapped in a red sweater from a shop photo, naming each reference by its job, so the model takes the clothes from one image and the man from the other.


Model: GPT Image 2.5 · Note: an edit with two references, the turnaround sheet and the sweater photo


```text
Man Character Reference Turnaround    is Man turnaround (Identity, face, glasses, hair, body proportions, four views and sheet layout).  Untitled Image    is Outfit reference (Red knit zip neck sweater, striped undershirt and dark trousers). Edit the man's four view character turnaround sheet by replacing his suit outfit in every view with the outfit in the clothing reference. Match the vivid red relaxed fit fine knit sweater with dropped shoulders, ribbed rounded neckline, ribbed cuffs and hem, and short silver front zipper partially open to reveal the black and cream horizontal striped crewneck shirt underneath. Replace suit trousers with dark navy trousers matching the clothing reference. Retain his existing black leather shoes. Remove the suit jacket, waistcoat, white shirt and tie entirely. Preserve exactly the man's face, age, glasses, hairstyle, proportions, neutral standing poses, full body front, left profile, back and right profile arrangement, plain gray background and realistic even studio lighting. Same outfit consistently across every view, with plausible plain red sweater back. Do not copy the clothing model's identity or hands in pockets pose. Preserve original sheet framing and photographic look. No text.
```


### 4. Build the first frame from your character and set


Zoey Z.


, director of[The Ghosted Boss](https://flick.art/film/the-ghosted-boss-383dd2)


· GPT Image 2.5


**What it is:** the opening image of the shot, made from the character sheet and the set.


**Why it matters:** the video model starts from this frame, so whatever is wrong here is wrong in every take.


How to do it


- Make an environment sheet for each location in your brief.
- Attach the character and the set, and say which reference gives what.
- List what not to take from each reference, so nothing leaks from one into the other.


With AI


One reference gives the man, the room and the grade. A second sets where he sits and how the table recedes, and the prompt rules out its suit, map, bookcase and golden grade.


Model: GPT Image 2.5 · Note: an edit with two references


```text
Man in Red Sweater, Meeting Room    is Red sweater man and meeting room (Man identity and outfit, meeting room design and vintage visual treatment).  Man at Conference Table    is Table placement reference (Centered far end subject position and lengthwise table framing only). Let the man wearing the red sweater sit in a chair at the far end of the conference table, in the same centered location as image 2's man, but keep image 1 visual. Use the red sweater man and meeting room image as the source of character identity, wardrobe, architecture, furnishings, lighting, color and photographic style. Reframe its meeting room looking straight down the length of its long wooden table, with table edges converging toward the man centered at the far short end, as in the table placement reference. He must be SITTING in an office chair facing the camera, not standing or leaning over the table. His seated torso and head are visible above the far edge, forearms resting naturally on the tabletop, lower body concealed by the table. Preserve his exact face, glasses, combed hair, red short zip neck sweater and striped undershirt. Remove his old foreground right position so there is only one man. Retain image 1's dark wood paneled walls, aluminum framed glass office partitions, brown upholstered office chairs, muted olive and yellow green palette, creamy highlights, matte shadows, diffuse interior illumination, fine analog grain and subtle vintage softness. Do not import image 2's suit, world map, bookcase, curtains, traditional executive office or golden high contrast grade. Image 2 supplies only centered subject placement and lengthwise perspective, not its standing pose. Wide cinematic 16:9 composition, realistic seated anatomy and scale, no additional people, no text.
```


### 5. Generate quick takes, then make the best one in full


00:30


Zoey Z.


, director of[The Ghosted Boss](https://flick.art/film/the-ghosted-boss-383dd2)


· Seedance 2.5 Draft


· Reference to video


**What it is:** fast draft versions of the shot, then one finished version of the take you choose.


**Why it matters:** the same prompt gives a different performance every time. Drafts let you find the one where the timing lands before you pay for the full take.


How to do it


- Attach the first frame and the sheets, paste the shot prompt, and generate.
- Watch for the timing of each line and the steadiness of the camera.
- Change one thing between takes, so you know what fixed it.


With AI


Zoey generated 10 takes of The Ghosted Boss with Seedance 2.5 Draft, then made the chosen one in full with Seedance 2.5 Final.


### 6. Reveal the product last, in the editor


00:08


Zoey Z.


· 0:22


**What it is:** the brand name, the interface and every word on screen, added in the edit in the last seconds.


**Why it matters:** viewers are already watching when they learn what the ad is for, and generated lettering warps.


How to do it


- Ask the model for no readable text in the footage.
- Add the logo, the product and any copy on top in the editor.
- Hold the reveal for the final beat.


With AI


In The Ghosted Boss, the AI team speaks in message bubbles animated in the Flick editor, and Pond's name arrives at the very end. Pond Marketing video's prompt keeps readable text out of every shot, and the words go on in the edit.
